llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Executable shell scripts and network access are visible in the artifact and match the documented CLI and hook design, though a richer structured permission declaration would improve platform transparency.
[SDI-2] expected: Auto-capture sends user and assistant turn text to the memory API only when the documented opt-in environment variable is enabled; this is privacy-sensitive but purpose-aligned and disclosed.
[SQP-2] expected: The pre-tool and post-tool hooks perform quiet HTTPS requests after opt-in, matching the advertised auto-recall and auto-capture behavior; users should understand there is no per-turn notice or redaction.
[E1] expected: External transmission through curl is the mechanism for hosted semantic memory search and storage, not an unrelated or hidden data path.
[PE3] expected: The optional plaintext credentials file is a real operational caution, but it is scoped to this service's API key and the setup guide recommends an environment variable first.
llm.guidance: Install only if you want a hosted memory service. Keep auto-capture and auto-recall off unless you are comfortable sending prompts, responses, and saved notes to Vanar Neutron over HTTPS, and avoid storing secrets, regulated data, or confidential business material unless that remote retention is acceptable. Prefer an environment variable or a tightly permissioned credentials file for the API key.
llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed hosted memory integration that sends saved text, search queries, and optionally conversation turns to Vanar Neutron when the user enables those features.
